title: A New World Order Is Not Beckoning
content: It does no good to get misty-eyed about the demise of the liberal international “order.” What the world really needs to manage today's biggest risks is a different, more realistic narrative that does not draw a sharp line between a disintegrating ideal and its post-liberal successor.

title: What It Means for Global Warming to Exceed 1.5°C
content: A sobering new report from the United Nations Environment Programme warns that even if governments deliver on all their existing climate pledges, warming could reach 1.8°C later this century. That means humanity must pivot from simply containing global warming to finding ways to reverse it.

title: Can Adaptation Accelerate Climate Action?
content: After a summer of apocalyptic headlines, a new survey finds that people across the political spectrum are deeply concerned about preparing for the effects of global warming. The adaptation imperative may end up being the kind of crisis that forces us to stop neglecting the green agenda and act at the necessary scale.

title: Africa’s AI Opportunity
content: The global AI revolution is often portrayed as a Sino-American race to develop the most advanced frontier models. But the greatest economic prize most likely will be found in deploying practical intelligence, particularly in Africa’s young, dynamic, and fast-growing economies.

title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock
content: For decades, Germany’s stability rested on an implicit bargain: high-value manufacturing would provide good jobs, strong export revenues, and broad-based prosperity, which political institutions would translate into social cohesion. Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.

title: When AI Stops Asking Permission
content: The most useful lesson from this summer’s breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents is about architecture, not intentions. AI agents need protective layers—limited access, separate authorization for sensitive actions, records nobody can quietly edit, and outside testing before deployment—not a lecture about good behavior.

content: Economic insecurity and growing distrust in institutions are undermining governments’ ability to sustain support for climate action. title: It’s Time to Reconsider Inflation Targeting
content: Central banks were caught off guard by the inflationary surge of 2021–23 because they relied too heavily on inflation forecasts based on flawed models and ignored other warning signs. Their failure to recognize the rapid growth of the money supply, in particular, underscores the need to reassess their reliance on inflation targeting.

title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
content: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
content: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
content: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

content: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system.
